issues.description: Return type for messageOnMilk is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem text/UML describes messageOnMilk as returning a boolean (indicating milking success), but the provided solution and referenced template usage implement and expect a String (e.g., "Seal X is milked"). This mismatch prevents students from knowing whether to implement a boolean-returning method (as described) or a String-returning method (as in the solution), and will cause compilation/test failures if they follow the wrong variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on a single return type for messageOnMilk and make all artifacts consistent. Either: (A) change the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk(): String (and update the textual description to show example strings), or (B) change the solution/template to implement messageOnMilk(): boolean and adjust the classes and tests accordingly. Prefer option (A) if the intended example outputs are string messages.

issues.description: Internal inconsistency in the problem statement UML: the Milkable interface is shown with messageOnMilk(): boolean while the Seal and Goat class boxes in the same UML show messageOnMilk(): String. This contradictory specification in the UML will confuse students about the correct signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the UML contradiction by making the Milkable interface and the class method signatures consistent. Update the UML so Milkable.messageOnMilk() and the Seal/Goat method entries all use the same return type (preferably String to match the solution and example outputs), and update any descriptive text that references the return semantics.
